text: Rutherford Chang began CENTS
with a simple value discrepancy.
What was one cent to the US Treasury
was about two and a half cents
as copper at the time he made the piece.
Nothing had been sold for a single cent since
before Chang was born, yet the object remained,
buoyed into physicality by the force of its context.
The readymade he chose is also perhaps
the most reproduced physical artwork on Earth.
More than 500 billion Lincoln cents
were produced, each with the portrait
of Lincoln that Victor David Brenner made in 1909.
It is absurd that a nation's currency
should dissolve into worthlessness.
It is absurd that a cent should be
valued at hundreds or thousands of dollars.
Yet here we are.
Chang brings a kind of black hole humor
to his work, laughing at this absurdity
with a laughter that resonates within emptiness.
In the system Chang created,
every cent is passed through
five transformations of value.
One, in circulation,
its value defined by the Treasury.
Two, removed from circulation,
that value assignment subverted.
Three, archivally photographed,
valued for what the image holds.
Four, destroyed, melted into a block
of copper, its value made undefinable.
Five, inscribed on Bitcoin,
its value continually redefined by decentralized
consensus as the objects are
traded every day on the open market.
CENTS is a becoming,
a gesture that unfolds continually
through the actions of
its participants through time.
